tagline: A courthouse town and a Dan River trading town in the Piedmont.
intro: The Colonial Heritage Byway reaches its northernmost point at Milton, just east of the Dan River. NC 62 connects Milton with Yanceyville, thirteen miles to the southwest. North Carolina DOT includes Colonial Heritage in its scenic-byway guide, whose routes are selected to represent the state’s geography, history and culture.

Milton’s earlier transport story followed the river: flatboats brought tobacco and corn to a prosperous trading center before the Civil War. In 1846, the town refused the Richmond and Danville Railroad permission to pass through, citing noise and other concerns.

In Yanceyville, the historic courthouse stands in Court Square. Northeast along NC 62 comes Milton, where NC 57 meets it in the town center. Farther south, Prospect Hill occupies the junction of NC 49 and NC 86 in southeastern Caswell County. Hillsborough lies along the Eno River, with surviving eighteenth- and nineteenth-century buildings.

moments.title: Yanceyville
moments.text: An octagonal cupola rises above the old Caswell County Courthouse, a stuccoed brick building on a granite foundation. Built between 1858 and 1861 with enslaved labor, it dates from the closing years of the county’s tobacco-driven boom. Its design combines Italian Romanesque and classical features. A new courthouse replaced it in the mid-1970s, a few blocks north of Court Square. The restored older building now provides offices for county departments. The building has a recessed entrance porch on two levels, beneath the cupola, with five bays across its front and seven along its depth.

moments.title: Milton
moments.text: Thomas Day, a free Black cabinetmaker, made his home and workshop in Milton’s Union Tavern. His woodwork also appears in the William Henry and Sarah Holderness House near Yanceyville. Milton’s prosperity before the Civil War rested on trade that brought tobacco and corn up the Dan River by flatboat. In 1846 the town turned away the Richmond and Danville Railroad, citing noise among its concerns. Union Tavern suffered severe fire damage in 1989. The town lies just east of the Dan, with the Virginia state line forming its northern boundary and NC 62 crossing the river.

moments.title: Prospect Hill
moments.text: NC 49 and NC 86 meet at Prospect Hill in southeastern Caswell County. Warren House and Warren’s Store were listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1973. Sugartree Creek, a tributary of South Hyco Creek, rises in the community.
